call_points.text: MTF book addition expected to continue at ₹600-700 Cr per quarter on average.
Cost to serve increased due to higher compute costs, AI investments, and a one-time expiry file delay hit.
SEBI's proposed CAS framework changes are not expected to materially impact derivatives as a segment.

penalties.details: The Company has received a letter dated June 30, 2026, from the National Stock Exchange of India Limited ("NSE") and BSE Limited ("BSE") levying penalty amount of Rs. 5,000/- (including 18% GST) each for delay in filing Disclosure of Related Party Transactions under Regulation 23(9) of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (Listing Regulations) for the Half-year ended March 31, 2026.
penalties.impact: The impact of the order is limited to the amount of levy under the order.

guidance.statement: MTF book expected to keep adding ₹600-700 Cr per quarter
Cash yields expected to rise a percentage point or two every quarter as MTF penetration increases
Cost to operate expected to continue as is with slight inflationary increase over coming quarters
Cost to Grow spend of roughly ₹400-500 Cr a year, with flexibility to spend more in a good market.

industry: Financial Services > Capital Markets > Stockbroking & Allied

events.client: RIBBIT CAYMAN GW HOLDINGS V LTD.

operating_notes.text: Total employee headcount stood at approximately 1,800 as of Q4 FY26.
MTF pricing is fixed at 14.95%, with reported yield varying slightly because of closing versus average balances.
LAS now makes up 34% of disbursements; commodities reached over 28% retail market share in notional ADTO.
Fisdom and AMC revenue together is under about 2% of total revenue, and Fisdom is still in gestation with no significant revenue improvement yet.
As at Sep-2026, ₹1,054.16 Cr of the ₹1,060 Cr IPO gross proceeds was utilised, leaving ₹5.84 Cr unspent (₹4.86 Cr issue expenses and ₹0.98 Cr GCP).
More than 50% of customers are using more than two products, and over 5% are using more than four products.
